He's carefully getting through the entire neighborhood's news of the day.
en.editorNote: Send to the owner who gets dragged to a halt at every single post on the walk — he isn't slow, he's reading the paper
variations: You think you're taking him out for exercise. Really, you're his internet, walking him online to scroll the whole block's feed.
The longer he sniffs, the juicier the post — some lampposts, he simply cannot stop reading.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年流行的「寵物越來越像主人」趨勢，改寫為原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
養久了，你會發現一件有點可怕的事：

牠開始變得跟你一樣。

你坐下來會嘆一口氣，牠現在趴下來也會嘆一口氣。
你每天下午三點半會想吃點什麼，牠三點二十五分就開始在廚房門口徘徊。
你滑手機的時候會癱成一個沒有骨頭的形狀，牠躺在旁邊，姿勢一模一樣。

最可怕的是那個表情——
你收到週五晚上八點的工作訊息時的那個表情，
牠看著窗外的鴿子時，居然也是那個表情。

人家說養狗養久了會越來越像，
我本來以為指的是臉。

後來我才知道，像的是靈魂。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個常被朋友說「你跟你家狗越來越像」的人
variations: 我一直以為是我在教牠規矩，直到有一天我發現，連我起身時那聲「唉唷」牠都學走了。
朋友來我家坐了五分鐘，只講一句話：你們兩個連坐姿都一樣，真的還需要做親子鑑定嗎？

en.content:
Live with a dog long enough and you notice something faintly alarming:

he's turning into you.

You sigh when you sit down; now he sighs when he lies down.
You get snacky around three-thirty; he starts loitering by the kitchen at three twenty-five.
You scroll your phone folded into a shape with no bones in it, and there he is beside you, in the exact same shape.

The worst part is the face —
the one you make when a work message lands at eight on a Friday night.
He makes that face at pigeons.

People say owners and dogs start to look alike.
I assumed they meant the face.

Turns out they meant the soul.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend everyone keeps telling: you and your dog are the same person now
variations: I thought I was the one teaching him manners, right up until he picked up the little grunt I make when I stand up.
A friend watched the two of us for five minutes and said: you even sit the same way. Are we still pretending a DNA test is needed?

items.sourceNote: 狗狗慢慢把主人擠出沙發位置的爆紅影片，改寫為原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
牠不會直接把你推下沙發，牠沒那麼粗魯。

牠用的是倒車。

先在你腳邊坐下，一臉「這不關我的事」。
三分鐘後，屁股往後挪兩公分。
再三分鐘，再兩公分。
每次你低頭看牠，牠都望向遠方，像在思考什麼很深的問題。

等你回過神，你已經坐在扶手上，
一隻手撐著牆維持平衡，
而牠橫躺在你原本的位置，四肢往四個方向攤開，睡得很沉。

全程沒有推、沒有擠、沒有任何暴力。
這叫和平演變。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個在自己家沙發上只分到二十公分的飼主
variations: 重點是牠躺好之後還會嘆一口氣，好像被擠的人是牠。
我研究出唯一的對策：起身前先放一顆抱枕佔位。牠三秒就把抱枕推到地上了。

en.content:
He won't shove you off the couch. He isn't that crude.

He reverse-parks.

First he sits by your feet, completely uninvolved.
Three minutes later, his backside shifts back two centimeters.
Three more minutes, another two.
Every time you look down, he's gazing into the middle distance like he's working through something profound.

By the time you catch on, you're perched on the armrest,
one hand against the wall for balance,
while he's laid out across your spot, all four legs pointing different directions, deeply asleep.

No pushing. No shoving. No violence at any point.
This is a peaceful transition of power.
en.editorNote: For anyone down to twenty centimeters of their own sofa
variations: And once he's settled, he sighs. As if he's the one being crowded.
I found exactly one countermeasure: put a pillow in my spot before standing up. He removed the pillow in three seconds.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗睏到站不穩仍堅持迎接主人回家的爆紅貼文，改寫為原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
加班到半夜一點，我很輕地開門，想說別吵到牠。

門一開，牠已經站在那裡了。

但牠其實沒有完全醒。
眼睛只睜開一半，站著站著身體慢慢往旁邊傾，差點撞到鞋櫃，又硬是把自己撐回來。
只有尾巴很誠實，一直搖，搖得比牠的意識還清醒。

我蹲下來說：你去睡啦，笨蛋。

牠把頭靠在我膝蓋上，就這樣睡著了。
任務完成，才准關機。

那一刻我突然覺得，加班到一點好像也沒那麼難熬。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個深夜才到家、卻有一隻狗撐著眼皮在等你的人
variations: 牠可以睡掉整個下午，卻堅持用一天之中最睏的狀態，親自確認你有平安回來。
我後來才懂：牠不是在等門，牠是在確認今天全員到齊，才肯真的睡。

en.content:
One in the morning, home from work. I ease the door open so I won't wake him.

The door opens. He's already standing there.

Except he isn't really awake.
Eyes half shut, he slowly tips sideways where he stands, nearly headbutts the shoe rack, then hauls himself upright again.
Only the tail is honest. It keeps wagging, more conscious than the rest of him.

I crouch down and tell him: go to bed, you idiot.

He rests his head on my knee and falls asleep right there.
Mission complete. Now he's allowed to power down.

Somehow, one a.m. stopped feeling so heavy.
en.editorNote: For everyone who gets home late and finds a dog fighting his own eyelids at the door
variations: He can sleep through an entire afternoon, yet he insists on confirming your safe return in the least conscious state available to him.
I understand it now. He isn't waiting by the door. He's waiting for everyone to be home before he lets himself really sleep.

items.sourceNote: 上班族偷看寵物攝影機、狗聽到對講喇叭到處找主人的梗，原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
我裝了寵物攝影機，本來是想知道牠白天到底在幹嘛。

觀察一個禮拜後，我整理出完整報告：

九點：睡。
十一點半：換一個地方睡。
下午兩點：起床，走三步，喝水，回去睡。
三點四十：對著一個空的牆角叫兩聲，原因不明。
四點：睡。

有一天我忍不住按了對講功能，說了聲：「乖喔——」

牠彈起來，衝到喇叭前面，繞三圈，抬頭看天花板，再看窗戶，
最後跑去門口坐好，一臉「把拔住在牆壁裡」的表情。

從那天起我再也不敢說話了。

倒是有一件事，我每天都在螢幕上看到：
我到家前十分鐘，牠會突然起身走到門口。
沒有人叫牠，也沒有任何聲音。

牠就是知道。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個上班偷看寵物攝影機、看著看著就開始想回家的飼主
variations: 牠一天的行程比我充實：睡、換位置睡、對空氣叫、繼續睡。而我在開會。
我最後把對講功能關掉了。因為牠找不到我的時候，會在門口坐很久很久。

en.content:
I installed a pet camera to find out what he actually does all day.

After a week of observation, I compiled a full report:

9:00 — asleep.
11:30 — asleep somewhere else.
14:00 — gets up, walks three steps, drinks water, returns to sleep.
15:40 — barks twice at an empty corner. Reason unknown.
16:00 — asleep.

One day I couldn't help myself and hit the two-way audio: 'Hey buddy—'

He launched upright, ran at the speaker, circled it three times, checked the ceiling, checked the window,
then went and sat by the front door with an expression that said dad lives inside the wall now.

I have never spoken through it again.

But there's one thing I see on that screen every single day:
ten minutes before I get home, he stands up and walks to the door.
Nobody called him. There's no sound.

He just knows.
en.editorNote: For everyone who checks the pet cam at work and ends up homesick before lunch
variations: His day is fuller than mine: sleep, relocate, sleep, bark at nothing, sleep. Meanwhile I'm in meetings.
I turned the speaker off in the end. When he can't find me, he sits by that door for a very long time.

items.sourceNote: 養狗後作息與運動量變規律的健康觀察，改寫為原創幽默語錄

zh-tw.content:
醫生說：你要多運動，一天至少走一萬步。
我點頭，回家繼續躺著。

後來我養了狗。

現在我一天走一萬兩千步，風雨無阻。

不是我變自律，是我請了一個不接受請假的教練。

下雨？牠站在玄關，牽繩已經叼在嘴上。
宿醉？牠不管，牠只知道現在七點了。
聚餐到一半？我看一下手錶，站起來說：抱歉我要回去遛狗——
這是我這輩子講過最有說服力的離場理由。

牠的鐘點費是三根肉條。
效果比我辦過的所有健身房會員卡加起來還好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個養狗之後莫名其妙變健康、作息也變正常的朋友
variations: 以前我的行事曆繞著會議排，現在繞著散步排。奇怪的是，我睡得比以前好。
健身房我去三次就放棄了，這位教練我跟了六年，一天都沒缺席。

en.content:
The doctor said: you need more exercise. Ten thousand steps a day, minimum.
I nodded, went home, and lay back down.

Then I got a dog.

Now I walk twelve thousand steps a day, in any weather.

It isn't discipline. I hired a trainer who doesn't accept time off.

Raining? He's at the door with the leash already in his mouth.
Hungover? Not his problem. It's seven o'clock and he knows it.
Halfway through dinner with friends? I check my watch, stand up and say sorry, I have to go walk my dog —
the most persuasive exit line I have ever owned.

His rate is three strips of jerky.
He outperforms every gym membership I have ever bought, combined.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who mysteriously got healthier the year they adopted a dog
variations: My calendar used to be built around meetings. Now it's built around walks. Strangely, I sleep better.
I quit the gym after three visits. I've been with this trainer for six years and he hasn't missed a day.

items.sourceNote: 飼主自己剪狗指甲、害怕剪到血線的普遍焦慮，改寫為原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
你買了一支寵物指甲剪，看了六支教學影片。
影片裡的人三分鐘剪完二十根，一氣呵成。

輪到你。

你把牠抱上膝蓋，翻開肉球，對著燈光找那條血線。
你看了很久。
你換一個角度，再看一次。
你決定先剪 0.5 公厘，比較安全。

「喀」——好，一根。
你深呼吸，放下指甲剪，去喝一口水。

牠全程躺得很平，眼睛半閉，偶爾抬頭看你一下，
那個眼神是：「你還好嗎？」

四十分鐘後，你剪完六根。
隔天，你打電話跟美容師預約。三分鐘，全部搞定，還附贈修腳底毛。

你在旁邊看著，覺得自己很沒用。
直到回家的路上你才想明白：
手會抖，不是因為技術差，是因為你太怕弄痛牠。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個買了指甲剪、最後還是每個月乖乖預約美容師的朋友
variations: 精簡版：教學影片三分鐘剪完二十根，我四十分鐘剪完六根，中間還休息兩次。
延伸版：那支指甲剪現在放在抽屜最裡面。它不是工具，是我當年很勇敢的紀念品。

en.content:
You bought the clippers. You watched six tutorials.
The people in the videos do all twenty nails in three minutes without blinking.

Then it's your turn.

You pull him onto your lap, spread the pad, hold the paw up to the lamp looking for the quick.
You look for a long time.
You change the angle and look again.
You decide to take off half a millimeter, just to be safe.

Click. Okay. One down.
You put the clippers down, breathe, and go get a glass of water.

He lies there flat the whole time, eyes half shut, lifting his head once in a while
with a look that says: are you okay?

Forty minutes later you have done six nails.
The next day you call the groomer. Three minutes, all of them, paw fur trimmed for free.

You stand there watching and feel a little useless.
It isn't until the drive home that it lands:
your hands shake because you can't stand the idea of hurting him. That's all it ever was.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who owns clippers and still books the groomer every single month
variations: Short version: the tutorial did twenty nails in three minutes. I did six in forty, with two breaks.
Longer version: those clippers live at the back of a drawer now. Not a tool — a souvenir from the day I was brave.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗喝完水濕下巴到處蹭的日常影片討論，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
牠喝水的方式裡，沒有「小口」這個選項。

舌頭像一台小型幫浦，水往三個方向噴，
五秒之內，碗的周圍會出現一圈完整的水漬地圖。

喝完，牠抬起頭，下巴掛著兩排水珠，滿意地看你一眼——

然後直直走過來，把那個濕下巴貼在你的膝蓋上。

你說「欸不要」，牠換另一邊，再貼一次。

這幾年你換過三種碗、四個位置，還買了一塊防濺墊。
最後你認清：問題不在碗，
是牠做任何事都不打算保留，連喝水都一樣。

你抱怨了六年，褲子濕了六年。
但你有沒有注意到——
牠喝完水，第一件想做的事，是先來找你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個褲子膝蓋永遠有一塊濕痕、還在研究要買哪種水碗的朋友
variations: 精簡版：牠喝水像在洗車，喝完再把多的水分還給我的褲子。
延伸版：我買了防濺墊，牠當成餐巾——喝完直接整張臉躺上去。

en.content:
There is no such thing as a small sip in his world.

His tongue works like a little pump. Water goes in three directions.
Within five seconds there is a complete map of splash around the bowl.

Then he lifts his head, two rows of droplets hanging off his chin, gives you a satisfied look —

and walks straight over to press that wet chin into your knee.

You say don't. He switches sides and does it again.

Over the years you have tried three bowls, four locations, and a splash mat.
Eventually you accept it: the bowl was never the problem.
He does nothing halfway, and that includes drinking.

Six years of complaining. Six years of damp jeans.
But have you noticed —
the first thing he wants to do after drinking is come find you.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend with a permanent damp patch on one knee who is still shopping for the perfect water bowl
variations: Short version: he drinks like he's washing a car, then returns the leftover water to my jeans.
Longer version: I bought a splash mat. He treats it as a napkin and lies face-down on it when he's done.

items.sourceNote: 毛巾擦臉／擦腳等日常照護習慣的參考，內容全為原創

zh-tw.content:
散步回來，你在玄關蹲下來，抽一張濕紙巾。

第一年：你得抓著牠的腳，牠一直抽走，你再抓回來。
第二年：你說「腳」，牠會停下來，勉強站好。
第三年——

你還沒開口。

牠走到玄關那塊墊子上，自己站定，
然後把右前腳抬起來，懸在半空中，等你。

右前腳擦完，牠換左前腳。
後腳牠不太喜歡，但還是給你。

沒有人教過牠這個順序，你也沒有真的訓練過。
那是你們兩個，一天一次，用六年慢慢磨出來的一條小規矩。

外面沒有人知道這件事。
但每天回家的那三十秒，你們有一個只有兩個人懂的儀式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每天在玄關蹲三十秒、把四隻腳擦乾淨才准進客廳的朋友
variations: 精簡版：我從來沒訓練過牠擦腳，但牠現在每天回家都自己先抬起右前腳。
延伸版：有一天我忘了擦，牠站在墊子上等了三分鐘。這條規矩，牠比我還認真在守。

en.content:
Back from the walk, you crouch in the entryway and pull out a wipe.

Year one: you had to hold the paw. He kept pulling it away. You kept taking it back.
Year two: you said "paw" and he would stop and more or less stand still.
Year three —

you don't say anything at all.

He walks onto the mat by the door, plants himself,
lifts his front right paw and holds it in the air, waiting for you.

Front right done, he switches to front left.
He isn't crazy about the back ones, but he gives them to you anyway.

Nobody taught him the order. You never really trained it.
It's one small rule the two of you wore into shape, once a day, over six years.

Nobody outside this apartment knows it exists.
But for thirty seconds every evening, you and he have a ritual only the two of you understand.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who crouches in the doorway every night wiping four paws before anyone is allowed on the rug
variations: Short version: I never trained him to do paws. He just lifts the front right one now, every time we get home.
Longer version: one night I forgot. He stood on the mat waiting for three minutes. He takes the rule more seriously than I do.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗寄宿寵物旅館後回家的反應與飼主罪惡感討論，內容為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
出發前一天，你在客廳收行李，牠在旁邊坐了一整晚。

你給寵物旅館寫了三頁交代：牠不吃紅蘿蔔、怕吸塵器、睡覺要有一件你的舊衣服。
對方笑著說沒問題，你還是又講了一次。

度假第二天，你人在海邊，第一件事是傳訊息問旅館「牠今天有沒有吃完」。
對方回你一張照片：牠趴在角落，很安靜。
你站在沙灘上看那張照片，看了大概五分鐘。

接牠回家那天，門一開——

牠不看你。
牠轉過頭去，屁股對著你。那三十秒，是牠這輩子唯一一次擺架子。

然後牠撐不住了。

牠衝過來，整隻撞進你懷裡，把頭埋進你外套裡不肯抬起來，
身上是旅館洗毛精的味道，你聞著覺得陌生，而且有點難受。

回家的車上牠睡得很沉。
你開得很慢，一路在想：下次不要去那麼多天了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個出國前寫了三頁狗狗說明書、在海邊還一直刷寵物旅館照片的朋友
variations: 精簡版：接牠回家那天，牠先背對我三十秒，然後整隻撞進我懷裡——架子只擺得住三十秒。
延伸版：牠身上有旅館洗毛精的味道，我隔天就幫牠洗澡。不是嫌香，是想把牠洗回我認得的樣子。

en.content:
The day before you leave, you're packing in the living room. He sits beside the suitcase all evening.

You hand the boarding place three pages of notes: he won't eat carrots, the vacuum terrifies him, he sleeps better with one of your old shirts.
They smile and say of course. You tell them one more time anyway.

Day two of the trip you're standing on a beach, and the first thing you do is message the kennel to ask whether he finished breakfast.
They send a photo back: him lying quietly in a corner.
You look at that photo in the sand for about five minutes.

Pickup day. The door opens —

and he won't look at you.
He turns his head away and gives you his back. Thirty full seconds. The only time in his life he has ever held a position.

Then he cracks.

He comes barreling over, slams into your chest, buries his face in your jacket and refuses to lift it.
He smells like their shampoo. You don't recognize the smell, and it bothers you more than it should.

He sleeps hard the whole ride home.
You drive slow, thinking: next time, fewer days.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who wrote a three-page care sheet before their trip and still refreshed the kennel's photo updates from the beach
variations: Short version: at pickup he turned his back on me for thirty seconds, then threw himself into my arms. That grudge had a very short shelf life.
Longer version: he came home smelling like their shampoo, so I bathed him the next day. Not because it smelled bad — because I wanted him to smell like ours again.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗暈車與車程焦慮的常見飼主經驗，改寫為原創語錄

zh-tw.content:
牠分得出方向盤往哪一邊轉。

巷口右轉，是河堤。牠會站起來，兩隻前腳搭在門邊，尾巴開始打節拍。
巷口左轉，是動物醫院。牠會慢慢坐下，看一眼窗外，再看你一眼，然後趴平。

你試過繞路。第一次有用。
第二次，牠在第三個紅綠燈就識破了。

後座鋪著一條舊毛巾，因為牠會暈車。
所以你開得比誰都慢，過彎放得很輕，冷氣調到不吹牠那一側。

有一天你只是要去加油。
你右轉，牠站起來了。你再右轉，尾巴又開始打節拍。

那天加完油，你多繞了十分鐘的河堤才回家。
沒有為什麼。
你只是不想讓那條尾巴停下來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了狗會暈車、開車開得比誰都慢的朋友
variations: 精簡版：右轉是河堤，左轉是醫院。我試過繞路，牠第三個紅綠燈就識破了。
延伸版：後座那條舊毛巾洗過八十次了。它比我車上任何一樣東西都重要。

en.content:
He can tell which way the wheel is turning.

Right at the corner means the river path. He stands up, front paws on the door, tail keeping time.
Left at the corner means the vet. He sits back down, glances out the window once, glances at you once, and lies flat.

You tried a different route. It worked exactly once.
The second time, he had it figured out by the third light.

There's an old towel on the back seat because he gets carsick,
so you drive slower than anyone on the road, ease into the turns, angle the vents away from his side.

One day you were only going to the gas station.
You turned right. He stood up. You turned right again, and the tail started keeping time.

You filled the tank and then drove ten extra minutes along the river before heading home.
No reason.
You just didn't want that tail to stop.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who drives twenty under the limit because their dog gets carsick
variations: Short version: right is the river, left is the vet. I tried a detour once — he busted me by the third traffic light.
Longer version: that old towel on the back seat has been washed eighty times. It's the most important thing in the car.

items.sourceNote: 獸醫診間量體重與飼主自我辯護的日常情境，內容全為原創

zh-tw.content:
護理師說：「來，上磅秤。」

牠超級配合。四隻腳站得整整齊齊，還抬頭看你一眼，一副「我表現很好吧」的樣子。

數字跳出來。

醫生看了看螢幕，再看看你：「比上次多了一點二公斤喔。」

你開始解釋。
你說你有在控制，你說零食都有算過，你說最近太熱、散步時間有縮短。
講到一半，你自己都不太信了。

旁邊那個被念的當事人，全程搖尾巴，完全不知道現在是在講牠。

回家路上你才想起來。
上禮拜牠站在廚房門口看你煎魚，那個眼神你撐了大概四秒。
前天牠自己乖乖走進浴室，你覺得這實在太懂事了，又多給兩塊。

一點二公斤。
沒有一克是牠自己拿的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次帶狗量體重都要在診間自我辯護三分鐘的朋友
variations: 精簡版：醫生說多了一點二公斤。我解釋到一半就心虛了——那些克數全部是我親手給的。
延伸版：現在我家零食罐上貼了一張紙條：「你不是在愛牠，你是在買自己安心。」

en.content:
"Up on the scale," the tech says.

He cooperates completely. Four feet squared up, head tipped toward you, the picture of a dog who knows he's nailing this.

The number comes up.

The vet looks at the screen, then at you. "He's up about two and a half pounds since last time."

You start explaining.
You say you've been watching it. You say the treats are all accounted for. You say it's been too hot for full walks.
Halfway through, you stop believing yourself.

Meanwhile the subject of the discussion is wagging away, entirely unaware that any of this is about him.

On the drive home it comes back to you.
Last week he stood in the kitchen doorway watching you cook fish. You held out roughly four seconds.
Two days ago he walked himself into the bathroom for a bath, and you decided that level of maturity was worth two extra biscuits.

Two and a half pounds.
Not one ounce of it was his idea.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who delivers a three-minute legal defense every time the vet mentions weight
variations: Short version: the vet said he was up two and a half pounds. I stopped believing my own excuses halfway through — every ounce came out of my hand.
Longer version: there's a sticky note on the treat jar now. It reads: this isn't love, this is you buying peace of mind.

items.sourceNote: 寵物晶片與名牌資料更新的重要性宣導，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
門只開了三秒。

你手上提著兩袋東西，用膝蓋頂著門，回頭的時候，玄關已經空了。

接下來那二十分鐘，你不記得自己是怎麼跑的。

你喊牠的名字，喊到聲音不像自己的。
你跑過公園、跑過那面牠每天一定要聞的圍牆、跑進巷口的便利商店，
問店員：「請問有沒有看到一隻——」講到一半你發現自己在發抖。

腦子開始播放那些最壞的畫面。
同時你在想：項圈名牌上的字，還看得清楚嗎？晶片登記的電話，是不是還停在舊的那一支？

第二十一分鐘，你在三號那棟後面的草地找到牠。

牠在追一隻蝴蝶。

看到你，牠很開心地跑過來，尾巴搖得像什麼事都沒發生。
對牠來說，也真的什麼都沒發生。

你蹲下來抱住牠，一個字都罵不出來。

那天晚上你做了兩件事：
訂了一個新名牌，把晶片資料裡的電話改成現在這一支。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每年都提醒大家「去更新晶片電話」的朋友——他一定親自活過那二十分鐘
variations: 精簡版：牠走失了二十分鐘。我找到牠的時候，牠在追一隻蝴蝶，尾巴搖得像什麼都沒發生。
延伸版：現在我家玄關貼著一張便條：關門，先看腳邊。那不是提醒，是那二十分鐘留下來的疤。

en.content:
The door was open for three seconds.

A bag in each hand, knee braced against the door, and when you turned around the entryway was empty.

You don't really remember how you ran for the next twenty minutes.

You called his name until your voice stopped sounding like yours.
You ran the park, the wall he has to sniff every single day, the convenience store on the corner,
asking the clerk "have you seen a—" and noticing halfway through the sentence that you were shaking.

Your brain started playing the worst footage it had.
Underneath that, a second track: is the tag on his collar still readable? Is the number on his microchip still the old one?

Minute twenty-one, you found him on the grass behind building three.

Chasing a butterfly.

He spotted you and came running, thrilled, tail going like nothing had happened.
From where he was standing, nothing had.

You knelt down and held onto him and couldn't get a single angry word out.

That night you did two things:
ordered a new tag, and updated the phone number on the chip.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who reminds everyone once a year to update their microchip number — they have lived those twenty minutes
variations: Short version: he was gone twenty minutes. I found him chasing a butterfly, tail wagging like nothing had happened.
Longer version: there's a note by our door now that says: close it, then check your feet. It isn't a reminder. It's a scar from those twenty minutes.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年手機／雲端儲存空間不足的普遍情境，結合毛主人視角原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
「儲存空間已滿。」

手機跳出這行字的時候，你按了「管理」，很有信心地想：清一清就好。

你先刪掉三個從來沒開過的 App。還是不夠。
你刪掉一堆截圖、發票、會議白板的照片。還是不夠。

最後你點進相簿，開始往下滑。

第一張，今年夏天，牠在陽台曬太陽，眼睛瞇成一條線。
再往下，去年冬天，牠鑽進棉被只露一顆頭。
再往下，那是牠剛到家的第二個禮拜，還那麼小，還不太敢看鏡頭。

你滑了四十分鐘。
一張都沒刪。

最後你去續了雲端方案，一個月九十九塊。

你很清楚自己買的不是空間。
你買的是——這些日子，可以再多留一份。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個寧可每月多付九十九塊、也刪不掉任何一張狗照片的朋友
variations: 精簡版：手機說儲存空間已滿。我滑了四十分鐘，一張都沒刪，最後乖乖去續了雲端。
延伸版：我真正怕的不是空間不夠，是有一天這些照片會變成我唯一還留得住的東西。

en.content:
"Storage full."

You tap Manage, feeling confident. A quick cleanup and you'll be fine.

You delete three apps you have never once opened. Not enough.
You delete a pile of screenshots, receipts, photos of whiteboards from meetings. Not enough.

So you open the photo library and start scrolling.

First one: this summer, him on the balcony in the sun, eyes squeezed into two thin lines.
Keep going: last winter, him under the comforter with nothing but a head sticking out.
Further down: his second week in the house, so small, still not quite brave enough to look at the camera.

You scroll for forty minutes.
You delete nothing.

Then you upgrade the cloud plan. Three dollars a month.

You know exactly what you're buying.
Not space. One more copy of these particular days.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who would rather pay every month forever than delete a single photo of their dog
variations: Short version: my phone said storage full. I scrolled for forty minutes, deleted nothing, and upgraded the plan.
Longer version: what scares me isn't running out of space. It's that one day these photos will be all I have left.

items.sourceNote: 颱風天狗狗拒絕在室內如廁、飼主只好冒雨出門的常見情境，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
窗外的風雨大到玻璃在抖。

你很有信心：今天不用出門。
你甚至提早在陽台鋪好尿布墊，還噴了誘導劑，覺得自己準備得很周全。

牠走過去，低頭聞了一下，抬起頭看你。
那個眼神翻譯出來是：「這是什麼？我不用這個。」

然後牠走到玄關，坐下，抬頭看著掛牽繩的那個鉤子。

你說：今天不行。
牠不動。
你說：真的不行，外面在颱風。
牠繼續坐著，那個姿勢像在等主公回心轉意，可以等到天亮。

第四十分鐘，投降的是你。

你穿雨衣、換雨鞋、拿傘——傘在你走出大門三秒後就開花了。
你們走到巷口那棵樹下，牠花了兩分鐘慎重挑位置，從容不迫。
全程四十五秒。

回到家，你們兩個都在滴水。
你蹲在浴室幫牠吹毛，牠一臉「今天散步也太短了」的不滿。

養狗才懂：
颱風假從來不是放給你的。
是放給牠，順便讓你有空陪牠淋雨。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個颱風天全副武裝出門、只為了讓狗在樹下站四十五秒的朋友
variations: 精簡版：我鋪好尿布墊、噴了誘導劑。牠聞一聞，抬頭看我一眼，然後走去玄關坐在牽繩底下。
延伸版：那天我傘開花、鞋子進水、整個人濕透。牠回家甩兩下就乾了，還嫌散步太短。

en.content:
The rain outside is hitting hard enough to rattle the glass.

You feel good about this one: nobody is going out today.
You even laid down a pee pad on the balcony ahead of time and sprayed the attractant stuff on it. Very prepared.

He walks over, sniffs it once, and looks up at you.
The look translates roughly to: what is this, and why would I use it.

Then he goes to the front door, sits down, and stares at the hook where the leash hangs.

You say: not today.
He doesn't move.
You say: seriously, there's a typhoon out there.
He keeps sitting, in the posture of someone prepared to wait until morning for you to come to your senses.

Minute forty, you're the one who folds.

Rain jacket, rain boots, umbrella — the umbrella turns inside out three seconds past the door.
You make it to the tree at the end of the alley, where he spends two full minutes selecting a spot, unhurried, deeply serious.
Total time: forty-five seconds.

You both drip your way back into the apartment.
You kneel in the bathroom with the dryer while he wears the expression of a dog who feels that walk was unacceptably short.

Only dog people know:
the storm day off was never yours.
It was his, and you got the afternoon free to stand in the rain with him.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who suited up in full rain gear so their dog could stand under a tree for forty-five seconds
variations: Short version: I set up the pee pad and sprayed the attractant. He sniffed it, looked at me, then went and sat under the leash hook.
Longer version: my umbrella flipped, my boots filled with water, I was soaked. He shook twice at the door and was dry, and still acted cheated on walk length.

items.sourceNote: 網路熱議「沒有人在乎狗主人叫什麼名字」的現象，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你在這個社區住了六年。
沒有人知道你叫什麼名字。

早上七點在公園，穿藍色外套的阿姨老遠就熱情地喊：「早安——」
她不是在跟你打招呼。她在看你腳邊那位。

這裡的人都是這樣被登記的。
你是「阿糖的把拔」。
賣早餐的太太知道牠不吃蛋。
轉角五金行的老闆，抽屜裡有一包專門留給牠的肉乾。
巷子另一頭那隻黃金叫多多。多多的媽媽叫什麼，你也不知道——她就是「多多的媽媽」，這樣就夠了。

有一次你自己出門買東西，沒帶牠。
三個人攔下你問：「今天怎麼一個人？」
沒有一個問你好不好。
他們問的都是同一句：「牠還好嗎？」

你笑一笑，說牠在家睡覺。

走回家的路上你才想通：
你在這裡不是沒有名字。
你有一個更好的——

你是牠的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在社區被叫了好幾年「某某的把拔」、卻一點都不介意的朋友
variations: 精簡版：住了六年，社區裡沒人知道我叫什麼。大家都叫我「阿糖的把拔」，老實說這個好聽多了。
延伸版：那天我自己出門，三個鄰居問我「牠還好嗎」，沒有一個問我好不好。我完全能理解他們。

en.content:
You've lived on this block for six years.
Nobody here knows your name.

Seven in the morning at the park, the woman in the blue jacket waves from forty feet away and calls out good morning.
She isn't greeting you. She's looking at the one standing by your ankle.

That's how everyone gets filed around here.
You are Sugar's dad.
The woman at the breakfast shop knows he won't touch egg.
The guy at the hardware store on the corner keeps a bag of jerky in his drawer, and it is not for any other dog.
There's a golden down the alley named Dodo. You have no idea what Dodo's mom is actually called either — she's Dodo's mom, and that has always been enough.

One day you ran an errand alone.
Three separate people stopped you: out by yourself today?
Not one of them asked how you were.
They all asked the same thing: is he okay?

You smiled and said he's home, asleep.

Halfway back you worked it out.
It isn't that you don't have a name here.
You have a better one.

You're his person.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who has been "so-and-so's dad" on their street for years and honestly prefers it
variations: Short version: six years on this block and nobody knows my name. I'm Sugar's dad, and frankly that title is an upgrade.
Longer version: I went out alone once and three neighbors asked if he was okay. None of them asked about me. Completely fair.

items.sourceNote: 老年犬居家環境調整（防滑、階梯、抬高食碗）的照護建議，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你沒有哪一天坐下來決定「牠老了」。
是家裡的東西，一件一件被換掉的。

先是沙發前面多了一個小台階。因為牠跳不上去了，卻又不肯認輸，每次硬跳落地那一聲，你聽了心臟會縮一下。
然後是地板。你把整條動線鋪上防滑墊，從牠的床一路鋪到水碗。客廳變得很醜，你完全不在乎。
接著水碗墊高了，因為牠低頭喝水，脖子會不舒服。
走廊裝了一盞小夜燈，因為牠半夜起來會撞到牆角。
散步的路線也短了：從河堤變成公園，再變成巷口那棵樹，來回。

有天朋友來家裡，看了一圈說：你家怎麼變成這樣？

你這才發現——
這幾年你不是在裝潢。
你是一格一格，把整個家搬到牠現在還走得動的地方。

牠慢下來，家就跟著慢下來。
這沒有什麼好委屈的。

牠年輕的時候，也是配合你的作息，
在門口等你下班，等了十年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了老狗把整個家鋪滿防滑墊、還覺得自己做得不夠的朋友
variations: 精簡版：我沒有哪一天決定牠老了。是沙發前多了台階、地板鋪了防滑墊、水碗墊高了、走廊多了一盞夜燈。
延伸版：朋友問我家怎麼變成這樣。我說我不是在裝潢，我是在把整個家，搬到牠還走得動的地方。

en.content:
There was never a day you sat down and decided he was old.
The house just changed, one object at a time.

First a little step appeared in front of the couch, because he couldn't make the jump anymore and refused to admit it, and the sound of him landing wrong made something in your chest tighten.
Then the floors. You ran non-slip mats along his whole route, from his bed all the way to the water bowl. The living room looks terrible. You do not care even slightly.
Then the bowl went up on a stand, because bending that far bothered his neck.
Then a small night light in the hallway, because he was clipping the corner on his way past at two in the morning.
The walk got shorter too: the river path became the park, and the park became the tree at the end of the alley and back.

A friend came over, looked around and said, what happened to your place?

And you realized:
you haven't been decorating for years.
You've been moving the entire house, piece by piece, to wherever he can still get to.

He slowed down, so the house slowed down.
There's nothing unfair about that.

When he was young he ran on your schedule,
waiting at the door for you to get home, for ten years straight.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who carpeted their whole apartment in non-slip mats for an old dog and still thinks it isn't enough
variations: Short version: no single day made him old. There was just a step by the couch, mats on the floor, a raised bowl, a night light in the hall.
Longer version: a friend asked what happened to my place. I said I'm not decorating. I'm moving the house to wherever he can still walk.

items.sourceNote: 寵物友善餐廳用餐的常見狀況與寵物餐點文化，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
你們去了一家寵物友善餐廳。

你點了一份義大利麵。
牠點了寵物餐：舒肥雞胸、南瓜泥、蒸花椰菜，擺盤還撒了一點起司粉，上面插了一支小旗子。

牠的餐比你的貴四十塊。
你的麵有點鹹。牠那塊雞胸嫩得不像話。

牠三口解決，然後轉頭開始看你的。

你放下叉子，非常認真地跟牠說：這個你不能吃，太鹹。
牠不接受這個說法。牠換了一個角度，繼續看。

隔壁桌的柯基一直想過來交朋友，牠假裝沒看到——
此刻牠全副心神只在你的盤子上。

結帳時店員問：「今天餐點還可以嗎？」
你說：「牠很滿意。」

你自己的呢？
沒吃完。因為後面那半小時，你都在跟一雙眼睛談判。

養狗才懂：
所謂寵物友善餐廳，就是一個你付錢、牠用餐、
你負責坐在對面看牠吃的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個帶狗出門吃飯、結果自己那盤冷掉的朋友
variations: 精簡版：牠的寵物餐比我的義大利麵貴四十塊，而且看起來好吃太多了。
延伸版：店員問餐點還可以嗎，我說「牠很滿意」。我自己的沒吃完，整頓飯都在跟一雙眼睛談判。

en.content:
You took him to one of those dog-friendly places.

You ordered pasta.
He ordered off the pet menu: sous-vide chicken breast, pumpkin puree, steamed broccoli, a light dusting of cheese, and a tiny flag stuck in the top.

His meal cost more than yours.
Yours was a little salty. His chicken looked absurdly tender.

He finished in three bites and immediately turned to study yours.

You set down your fork and explain, very sincerely, that he cannot have this, it's too salty.
He declines to accept that. He shifts to a better angle and resumes staring.

A corgi at the next table keeps trying to make friends. He pretends not to notice.
His entire attention budget is allocated to your plate.

At the register the server asks how everything was.
You say: he was very happy with it.

Yours?
Unfinished, because you spent the last half hour negotiating with a pair of eyes.

Only dog people know:
a dog-friendly restaurant is a place where you pay, he dines,
and your job is to sit across from him and watch.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose own food went cold at the dog-friendly brunch place
variations: Short version: his pet-menu plate cost more than my pasta and looked significantly better.
Longer version: the server asked how the meal was and I said he loved it. Mine went unfinished — I spent the whole time negotiating with a pair of eyes.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗第一次下水的漸進式引導方式與常見反應，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
大家都說，狗天生就會游泳。

所以你買了救生衣、防水玩具，挑了一個人比較少的下午。
你把牠抱到最淺的那一區，四隻腳一碰到水，整隻僵住，眼睛瞪得像看見鬼。

前二十分鐘，牠在岸邊來回踱步，像個很有原則的監工。
你自己下水，游到中間回頭喊牠。
牠站在岸上叫得很大聲，意思很清楚：「你上來，那裡很危險。」

第三十五分鐘，你拿出雞肉條。
牠下水了。

牠確實天生就會——狗爬式標準到可以拍教學影片。
問題是方向。
牠用盡全力、一路直線，游回岸上。
全程四十公分。

上岸後甩了三次水，重新回到崗位，繼續監督你。

回程車上，牠裹在浴巾裡睡得很沉，鼻頭還在滴水。
你看了一眼後照鏡，決定下禮拜再帶牠來。

養狗才懂：
不是每件你花錢準備的事牠都會喜歡。
但只要你在水裡，牠一定會在岸上等你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個買了狗狗救生衣、結果整個下午只有自己下水的朋友
variations: 精簡版：牠天生就會游泳，狗爬式很標準。問題是牠只游一個方向——回岸上，全程四十公分。
延伸版：我在水裡游，牠在岸上叫，像個很有原則的救生員。回程牠裹著浴巾睡死，我決定下禮拜再帶牠去一次。

en.content:
Everyone says dogs are born knowing how to swim.

So you bought the life vest, the floating toy, and picked a quiet afternoon.
You set him down in the shallowest corner. All four feet touch water and he freezes solid, eyes wide as saucers.

For the first twenty minutes he paces the edge like a foreman with strong opinions about safety.
You get in yourself, swim to the middle, and call him.
He stands on the bank and barks, and the meaning is unmistakable: come back, that place is dangerous.

Minute thirty-five, you produce the chicken strips.
He gets in.

And he really was born knowing — the paddling is textbook, film-it-for-a-tutorial good.
The problem is the heading.
He swims flat out, in a perfectly straight line, back to shore.
Total distance: sixteen inches.

He shakes three times, resumes his post, and goes back to supervising you.

On the drive home he's wrapped in a towel, asleep harder than he's ever slept, nose still dripping.
You check the mirror once and decide you're bringing him back next weekend.

Only dog people know:
not everything you spend money preparing is something he'll enjoy.
But if you're in the water, he will be on the bank, waiting.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who bought a dog life vest and ended up swimming alone all afternoon
variations: Short version: he really was born knowing how to swim. Perfect form. He just only swims one direction — back to shore, sixteen inches.
Longer version: I swam, he barked from the bank like a lifeguard with strong safety opinions. He slept the whole drive home in a towel. We're going back.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗吃草行為的常見說法與飼主反應，內容全為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
散步走到一半，牠停下來，開始吃草。

不是隨便一叢，是那一叢。
前面兩叢牠聞過就走，第三叢牠低頭認真咀嚼，像在挑自助餐。

你當下什麼都沒說。

但那天晚上十一點半，你躺在床上，手機的光打在臉上，搜尋列裡輪流打著：
「狗 吃草 正常嗎」
「狗 吃草 腸胃不舒服」
「狗 吃草 需要看醫生嗎」

你看完六篇文章、兩支影片、一整串論壇留言。
有人說是纖維不夠，有人說是想吐，有人說是無聊，
有人說：「我家的吃了十四年，活到十六歲。」

凌晨十二點四十，你關掉手機，翻過身。

牠躺在床邊的墊子上，四腳朝天，打呼。

養狗才懂：
牠隨便做一個小動作，你就要研究一個晚上。
而當事人早就睡著了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了狗一個小動作，半夜爬文爬到一點的朋友
variations: 精簡版：牠白天吃了一口草，我晚上查了六篇文章、兩支影片。牠本人在旁邊打呼。
延伸版：論壇裡有人說缺纖維、有人說想吐、有人說「我家的吃了十四年活到十六歲」。我決定相信最後那個。

en.content:
Halfway through the walk he stops and starts eating grass.

Not just any patch. That patch.
He sniffed two others and walked on. The third one he chews with real attention, like a man working a buffet.

You don't say anything at the time.

But at eleven thirty that night you're lying in bed with the phone lighting up your face, typing, in order:
is it normal for dogs to eat grass
dog eating grass upset stomach
dog eating grass should I call the vet

You get through six articles, two videos, and an entire forum thread.
One person says fiber. One says nausea. One says boredom.
One says: mine ate grass for fourteen years and lived to sixteen.

At 12:40 you put the phone down and roll over.

He's on the mat beside the bed, feet in the air, snoring.

Only dog people know:
he does one small thing and you lose a whole night researching it.
Meanwhile the subject of the investigation is already asleep.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who stayed up until one reading forums about one thing their dog did
variations: Short version: he ate one mouthful of grass in the afternoon. I read six articles and watched two videos about it that night. He snored through all of it.
Longer version: the forum said fiber, or nausea, or boredom, or "mine ate grass for fourteen years and lived to sixteen." I chose to believe the last guy.

items.sourceNote: 正向獎勵訓練中狗狗把動作與零食連結的行為現象，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你花了一個月教會牠「握手」。
你以為你教的是服從。

牠學到的是：做這個動作，會有東西吃。

所以現在，只要你的手伸向零食櫃，牠就自動開始跑流程——
坐下、握手、換另一隻手、趴下、翻身、裝死，
一氣呵成，中間不需要任何指令。

你一個字都還沒說。
牠已經全套演完，抬頭看你，一臉「該你了」。

有時候你只是去拿自己的餅乾。
牠照樣完整表演一次。
你只好在心裡跟牠道歉，然後偷偷從櫃子裡摸一小塊給牠。

你以為那一個月是在訓練牠。
其實你們簽的是一份雙向合約，
而那份合約的條款，牠比你早八年就看懂了——
而且對牠比較有利。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個零食櫃一打開、狗就自動表演全套才藝的朋友
variations: 精簡版：我手伸進零食櫃，牠就自動跑完坐下、握手、趴下、翻身、裝死。我一個字都還沒講。
延伸版：有時候我只是去拿自己的餅乾，牠照樣全套演完。最後拿到東西吃的還是牠。

en.content:
You spent a month teaching him to shake.
You thought you were teaching obedience.

What he learned was: do this thing, food appears.

So now, the moment your hand moves toward the treat cabinet, he starts running the program —
sit, shake, other paw, down, roll over, play dead,
the whole sequence, no commands required.

You haven't said a word.
He's already finished the set and is looking up at you like: your move.

Sometimes you're just getting your own crackers.
He performs the full routine anyway.
You apologize internally, then quietly take one small thing out of the cabinet for him.

You thought that month was you training him.
What you actually signed was a two-way contract,
and he understood the terms about eight years before you did —
and they favor him.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose dog runs its entire trick repertoire the second the treat cabinet opens
variations: Short version: my hand moves toward the treat cabinet and he runs sit, shake, down, roll over, play dead. I haven't said anything.
Longer version: sometimes I'm just getting my own snack. He does the full routine regardless. He is still the one who ends up eating.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗散步途中頻繁回望確認飼主位置的行為（check-in），情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
散步的時候，牠永遠走在前面。

尾巴翹著，步伐比你快，每一根電線桿都要停。
看起來一點都不需要你。

但你有沒有注意過——
每走十幾步，牠會回頭。

不是停下來，也不是在叫你。
就是很快看你一眼，確認你還在那個位置，然後轉回去繼續走。

過馬路前看一次。
轉彎的時候看一次。
遇到不認識的狗，先看你，再決定要不要靠近。

牠不是在等你跟上。
牠是在確認你沒有不見。

有一天你故意躲到轉角後面，想看看牠多久才會發現。
三秒。
牠回頭，看到那個位置空了，整隻定住，然後往回跑——
跑得比你這輩子看過的任何一次都急。

你趕快走出來。
牠撞上你的腿，鼻子一直頂你，像在確認你是真的。

那天之後，你再也沒躲過。

養狗才懂：
牠敢走在前面，是因為牠相信你會在後面。
這種信任，不適合拿來開玩笑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個以為狗散步時完全沒在看自己的朋友
variations: 精簡版：牠走在前面，每十幾步回頭看我一眼。不是等我跟上，是確認我沒有不見。
延伸版：我躲到轉角後面，三秒牠就發現了，然後用這輩子最急的速度跑回來。之後我再也沒躲過。

en.content:
On walks he's always out in front.

Tail up, moving faster than you, stopping at every pole.
He looks like someone who does not need you at all.

But have you ever noticed —
every dozen steps, he glances back.

He doesn't stop. He isn't calling you.
It's a fast look, confirming you're still in the spot where you're supposed to be, and then he faces forward again.

Once before a crosswalk.
Once at every corner.
When a strange dog appears, he checks you first, then decides whether to go say hi.

He isn't waiting for you to catch up.
He's making sure you haven't disappeared.

One day you duck behind a corner on purpose, just to see how long it takes him to notice.
Three seconds.
He looks back, sees the empty spot, goes completely still, and then runs —
faster than you have ever seen him move in his life.

You step out immediately.
He crashes into your legs and keeps pushing his nose at you, confirming you're real.

You never did it again.

Only dog people know:
he walks in front because he believes you'll be behind him.
That kind of trust isn't something to joke around with.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who thinks their dog isn't paying attention to them on walks
variations: Short version: he walks ahead and glances back every dozen steps. Not waiting for me to catch up — checking that I haven't disappeared.
Longer version: I hid behind a corner and he noticed in three seconds, then ran back faster than I've ever seen him move. I never did it again.

items.sourceNote: 狗狗疼痛的細微行為訊號（舔嘴、打哈欠、聞空氣、活動力下降）常被飼主忽略，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
牠不會喊痛。

這是養狗最難的一件事。

踩到碎玻璃會叫，被門夾到會叫——那種痛你看得出來。
但慢慢累積的那種，牠不會說。

牠只會：
一直舔嘴唇，你以為牠在想吃的。
一直打哈欠，你以為牠想睡了。
抬起頭對著空氣聞很久，你以為隔壁在煎魚。
玩到一半突然停下來，你以為牠今天比較懶。

這些訊號小到沒有人會把它跟「痛」連在一起。

有一次，牠連續三天沒去追那顆球。
你想說牠長大了、穩重了，還跟朋友開玩笑說我家狗最近很有禪意。

第四天帶牠去打預防針，醫生順手壓了一下牠的後腳，牠縮了一下。
片子照出來，那個關節已經痛一陣子了。

你走出診間，腦袋一直重播那三天。

牠不是變穩重。
牠是在忍。
而牠忍著的那三天，還是每天走到門口迎接你，尾巴照搖，一次都沒少。

養狗才懂：
牠不會告訴你哪裡痛，牠只會安靜地把痛收起來，繼續當那隻很愛你的狗。
所以「看懂牠」這件事，本來就是我們這邊要做的功課。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給覺得「牠沒叫就代表沒事」的狗爸媽，也適合提醒自己定期帶牠健檢
variations: 精簡版：牠不會喊痛。牠只會突然不想玩、一直舔嘴唇、對著空氣聞很久。那些小動作，是牠唯一說得出口的話。
延伸版：牠三天沒追球，我以為牠變穩重了。照了片才知道牠已經痛一陣子。牠不是變穩重，牠是在忍——而且忍著的時候，還是每天到門口接我。

en.content:
He will never tell you it hurts.

That's the hardest part of loving a dog.

Glass in a paw, a tail caught in a door — that kind of pain you can see.
The kind that builds up slowly, he keeps to himself.

All he does is:
lick his lips over and over, and you assume he's thinking about food.
Yawn again and again, and you assume he's sleepy.
Lift his head and sniff the air for a long time, and you assume someone's cooking next door.
Stop in the middle of playing, and you assume he's just lazy today.

These signals are so small that nobody connects them to pain.

One week he went three days without chasing his ball.
You decided he was maturing. Settling down. You even joked to friends that your dog had gotten very zen lately.

On day four you took him in for shots, the vet pressed his back leg almost absent-mindedly, and he flinched.
The images came back. That joint had been hurting for a while.

You walked out of the clinic replaying those three days on a loop.

He wasn't settling down.
He was enduring it.
And during those three days he still walked to the door to meet you every single time, tail going, never once skipping it.

Only dog people know:
he won't tell you where it hurts. He'll quietly put the pain away and go on being the dog who loves you.
Which means learning to read him was always our job, not his.
en.editorNote: Send to anyone who assumes a quiet dog is a healthy dog — and as a nudge to book that checkup
variations: Short version: he'll never say it hurts. He'll just stop wanting to play, lick his lips a lot, sniff the air too long. Those tiny things are the only words he has.

Longer version: he skipped his ball for three days and I thought he was maturing. The scan said he'd been in pain for a while. He wasn't maturing — he was enduring it, and still met me at the door every night.

items.sourceNote: 研究指出狗會讀取飼主情緒，飼主開心時狗在任務上表現更好；情境與文字皆為原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
你今天心情很差，但你什麼都沒說。

同事沒看出來。家人問你怎麼了，你說沒事。
連你自己都覺得藏得挺好的。

只有牠不對勁。

牠沒有像平常那樣叼東西過來煩你。
牠走到你旁邊趴下，過三十秒又站起來，換一個角度再趴一次。
一整個晚上牠沒睡熟過，每隔幾分鐘就抬頭，確認你還在原來的位置。

你隨口叫牠做那個平常一秒就會的動作，牠做得歪歪的，做完立刻抬頭看你的臉，像在問「這樣可以嗎」。

你這才發現一件事——

你的情緒對牠來說不是背景音，是天氣。

你笑，牠的世界就是晴天，什麼都學得會，尾巴打在地板上啪啪響。
你一緊繃，牠整隻縮小一號，連走路都放輕。

牠不知道你在煩什麼。
牠只知道，那個決定牠一整天好壞的人，今天狀態不對。

你最後把手放到牠背上，很慢地吐了一口氣。
牠這才「呼」的一聲整個攤下去，兩秒鐘就睡著了。

養狗才懂：
家裡有一隻狗，你就沒辦法真的假裝沒事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配狗狗擔心地盯著你的照片，傳給那個什麼事都說「我沒事」的朋友
variations: 精簡版：我心情差什麼都沒說，只有牠整晚沒睡熟，每隔幾分鐘抬頭確認我還在原位。
延伸版：我的情緒對牠來說不是背景音，是天氣。我笑，牠什麼都學得會；我一緊繃，牠連走路都放輕。

en.content:
You were in a bad mood today and you didn't say a word about it.

Your coworkers didn't notice. Your family asked what was wrong and you said nothing's wrong.
You honestly thought you were hiding it well.

Only the dog was off.

He didn't bring you anything to throw the way he always does.
He lay down next to you, stood up thirty seconds later, and lay down again facing a slightly different way.
All evening he never fell properly asleep. Every few minutes his head came up to check you were still in the same spot.

You asked him for the cue he can normally do in one second. He did it crooked, then looked straight up at your face like he was asking, is this okay?

And that's when it landed —

your mood isn't background noise to him. It's weather.

You laugh and his world is a clear day: he learns anything, tail slapping the floor.
You tense up and he shrinks a size, walking softer than usual.

He has no idea what you're worried about.
He only knows the person who decides whether his whole day is good is not okay tonight.

Eventually you put a hand on his back and let out one slow breath.
Only then does he flop over with a sigh and fall asleep in about two seconds.

Only dog people know:
with a dog in the house, you don't actually get to pretend you're fine.
en.editorNote: Pair with a photo of your dog staring at you with worried eyebrows; send to the friend whose default answer is "I'm fine"
variations: Short version: I said nothing about my bad day. The dog just never fell asleep, lifting his head every few minutes to check I hadn't moved.
Longer version: my mood isn't background noise to him, it's weather. I laugh and he can learn anything; I tense up and he even starts walking quieter.

items.sourceNote: 居家幫狗刷牙的常見過程與飼主心態轉變，情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
獸醫說：狗狗最好每天刷牙。

聽起來很合理。你買了寵物牙刷、雞肉口味的牙膏，還認真看完教學影片。

第一天：你擠一點牙膏讓牠舔。牠舔得超開心，尾巴狂搖。你心想，這也太順利了吧。

第二天：你把牙刷拿出來。牠看了牙刷一眼，看了你一眼，然後很有禮貌地把頭轉開，意思是「那個不行」。

第三天起，正式進入攻防戰。
你左手抱住牠，右手拿牙刷。
牠的頭可以在原地轉出你這輩子沒看過的角度。
那天你刷到的東西包括：牠的鼻子、你自己的手指、牠的耳朵內側，以及大量的空氣。
牠的犬齒，一次都沒碰到。

第七天，你終於刷到兩顆後面的臼齒，興奮到差點發限時動態。

第十四天，你突然想通一件事：
牠根本不是在抵抗。
牠是在跟你玩。
牙刷在牠眼裡不是牙刷，是一個會動的、有雞肉味的新玩具。

所以你放棄了「刷乾淨」這個目標，改成「每天一定要玩到這個遊戲」。
奇怪的是，從那天開始，牠自己會在晚上走到浴室門口等。

三個月後回診，醫生說牙結石少了很多。
你在診間裡差點哭出來。

養狗才懂：
很多事你贏不了牠，你只能改規則。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在跟毛孩打刷牙攻防戰、覺得自己快放棄的朋友
variations: 精簡版：幫狗刷牙第七天，我終於刷到兩顆後臼齒，興奮到差點發限時動態。
延伸版：後來我才發現牠不是在抵抗，是在玩。牙刷對牠來說是一個會動、有雞肉味的玩具。於是我放棄刷乾淨，改成每天一定要玩到這個遊戲——結果牠開始自己去浴室門口等。

en.content:
The vet said dogs should get their teeth brushed daily.

Sounds reasonable. You bought the dog toothbrush, the chicken-flavored paste, and watched the whole tutorial.

Day one: you squeeze out a little paste and let him lick it. He loves it. Tail everywhere. You think, well, this is going great.

Day two: you produce the toothbrush. He looks at the brush. He looks at you. Then he politely turns his head away, meaning: that part, no.

From day three it's open warfare.
Left arm around him, brush in your right hand.
His head can rotate to angles you have never witnessed on a living animal.
Things you successfully brushed that day: his nose, your own fingers, the inside of his ear, and a great deal of open air.
His canines: zero contact.

Day seven you finally get two back molars and you're so proud you almost post about it.

Day fourteen it hits you:
he isn't fighting you.
He's playing with you.
The toothbrush was never a toothbrush to him. It's a new toy that moves and tastes like chicken.

So you drop the goal of "clean teeth" and replace it with "we have to play this game every night."
Oddly enough, that's when he started waiting outside the bathroom door on his own.

Three months later the vet says the tartar is way down.
You nearly cry in the exam room.

Only dog people know:
there are a lot of things you can't win against him. You can only change the rules.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend currently losing the nightly toothbrushing battle and thinking about quitting
variations: Short version: day seven of brushing my dog's teeth, I finally reached two back molars and nearly posted about it.

Longer version: turns out he wasn't resisting, he was playing. The brush is a toy that moves and tastes like chicken. So I stopped aiming for clean teeth and started aiming for the game — and then he began waiting by the bathroom door himself.

items.sourceNote: 部分狗狗需要飼主在場才願意進食的行為（social facilitation），情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你把飯倒進碗裡，端到牠固定的那個位置。

牠沒有衝過去。

牠跑來找你。
用鼻子頂一下你的小腿，往廚房的方向走兩步，回頭確認你有沒有跟上。
你要是沒動，牠會再回來頂一次，力道加倍。

你走過去，站在旁邊，牠才低頭開始吃。

你試過偷偷走掉。
走到第三步，身後的咀嚼聲就停了。
你回頭，牠站在碗前面看著你，嘴巴裡還含著一口沒吞。

一開始你覺得很煩。飯都幫你放好了，還要人站崗。
你甚至上網查過這是不是什麼分離焦慮。

後來你才想通——

在牠的邏輯裡，吃飯不是一個人的事，是全家一起做的事。
你不在，那這頓飯就還沒開始。

現在你養成習慣了：牠吃飯的那三分鐘，你就靠著流理台滑手機。
偶爾牠會抬頭看你一眼，確認你還在，然後低頭繼續。

三分鐘而已。
但那是牠一天當中，最確定「大家都在」的三分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給不懂為什麼有些狗吃飯一定要人陪的朋友，也適合配飯碗照
variations: 精簡版：飯都倒好了牠不吃，先跑來頂我的小腿，把我帶到廚房，等我站定牠才開始吃。
延伸版：在牠的邏輯裡，吃飯是全家一起做的事。我不在，那這頓飯就還沒開始。所以那三分鐘我都靠著流理台陪牠站著。

en.content:
You pour the food, set the bowl down in his usual spot.

He doesn't run to it.

He comes to find you.
Nudges your shin with his nose, walks two steps toward the kitchen, looks back to see if you're following.
If you haven't moved, he comes back and nudges again, harder.

You walk over. You stand there. Only then does he lower his head and start eating.

You've tried sneaking off.
By your third step the chewing behind you stops.
You turn around and he's standing over the bowl watching you, one mouthful still unswallowed.

At first this annoyed you. The food is right there and he needs a chaperone.
You even looked up whether it counted as separation anxiety.

Then it clicked —

in his logic, eating isn't something you do alone. It's something the family does together.
If you're not there, dinner hasn't started yet.

So now it's a habit: for those three minutes you lean against the counter and scroll your phone.
Every so often he glances up to confirm you're still there, then goes back down.

It's three minutes.
But it's the three minutes of his day when he's most certain that everybody is home.
en.editorNote: Send to anyone confused about why some dogs won't eat unless a human is standing there; works well with a photo of the bowl
variations: Short version: the food is already down and he won't touch it — he comes and nudges my shin first, walks me to the kitchen, and only starts once I'm standing there.
Longer version: in his logic, eating is something the family does together. If I'm not there, dinner hasn't started yet. So I spend those three minutes leaning on the counter.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 AI 寵物翻譯項圈／人狗對話項圈的新聞熱潮；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你花了三千多塊，買了那個號稱能把狗叫聲翻成人話的 AI 項圈。

說明書寫得很厲害：一百萬筆聲紋、準確率九成四。

夾上去的第一天，你盯著手機看了一整晚。

早上七點：「餓。」
七點零三分：「餓。」
七點零五分：「餓。」

中午你出門買午餐，回來看紀錄：「你去哪裡。」「你去哪裡。」「你去哪裡。」

下午牠對著窗外叫了兩聲，翻譯是：「有人來了。」

晚上你坐在沙發上滑手機，牠趴在你腳邊，整整一個小時，一筆紀錄都沒有。

你有點失望。三千塊耶。

然後你低頭看了牠一眼。

牠也正好抬頭看你。

那一秒你忽然懂了——

機器沒有翻錯，也沒有壞掉。
是牠這輩子想說的話，本來就只有那幾句。

餓、你去哪裡、有人來了、你在。

而最後那一句，牠從來不需要用叫的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看到寵物翻譯器就手癢想下單的朋友——先看完這段再決定要不要刷卡
variations: 精簡版：買了 AI 狗語翻譯項圈，一整天的紀錄只有三句：餓、你去哪裡、有人來了。牠趴在我腳邊那一小時，機器一片空白。
延伸版：三千塊買一台翻譯機，最後翻出來的結論是——牠這輩子想講的話本來就只有那幾句，而最重要的那句不用翻。

en.content:
You spent real money on the collar that claims to turn barks into sentences.

The box is very confident: a million voice samples, 94% accuracy.

The first day you clipped it on, you watched your phone all evening.

7:00 a.m. — "Hungry."
7:03 — "Hungry."
7:05 — "Hungry."

You step out for lunch. You come back to the log: "Where did you go." "Where did you go." "Where did you go."

Afternoon, two barks at the window: "Someone's here."

That night you're on the couch scrolling and he's stretched across your feet, and for a full hour the app records nothing at all.

You feel a little cheated. That thing was not cheap.

Then you look down at him.

He happens to look up at you.

And it lands —

the device isn't broken and it isn't wrong. There were only ever a few things he wanted to say.

Hungry. Where did you go. Someone's here. You're here.

And that last one he has never once needed to say out loud.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose finger is hovering over the buy button on a pet translator — let them read this first
variations: Short version: bought the AI bark translator. Full day of logs, three sentences: hungry, where did you go, someone's here. The hour he spent lying on my feet, the app had nothing.
Longer version: I paid for a translator and what it proved is that there were only ever a few things he wanted to say — and the most important one doesn't need translating.

items.sourceNote: 老犬聽力退化的常見徵兆（叫不動、從背後靠近會受驚、對零食袋聲音沒反應）與飼主應對方式；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你在廚房捏了一下零食袋。

那個聲音，過去十二年只要響一次，牠會從家裡任何一個角落用滑壘的姿勢出現。

這次沒有。

你又捏了一下，大聲一點。客廳還是沒有動靜。

你走過去。牠睡在牠那張墊子上，胸口一起一伏，睡得很好。
你蹲下來，手放到牠肩膀上——牠嚇得整隻彈起來，看清楚是你，耳朵才慢慢放平。

那天晚上你查了很多資料。
原來牠不是變不聽話。

現在你回家不會在門口喊牠的名字了。
你會先開燈，讓光掃過牠的眼睛。
走近牠之前，你會用腳在地板上踩兩下，讓震動先到，你再到。
叫牠吃飯改成揮手，出門散步改成把牽繩舉高給牠看。

牠學得比你快。你才是那個花了三個月才習慣的人。

有一天你在牠旁邊坐下，牠把下巴放到你腿上。
你忽然想到：牠已經聽不見這個世界了。

但牠還是每天在門口等你。

那代表牠等的，從來就不是聲音。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給家裡狗狗最近開始「叫不動」的朋友——那不一定是老番顛，先帶去檢查耳朵；也適合提醒自己換一套溝通方式
variations: 精簡版：牠不是變不聽話，是聽不見了。現在叫牠吃飯改成揮手，走近牠之前先在地板踩兩下，讓震動先到，我再到。
延伸版：牠已經聽不見這個世界了，但還是每天在門口等我。那代表牠等的從來不是聲音。

en.content:
You crinkle the treat bag in the kitchen.

For twelve years that sound has produced a dog sliding around the corner from anywhere in the house.

Not this time.

You do it again, louder. Still nothing from the living room.

You walk over. He's asleep on his mat, chest rising and falling, perfectly content.
You crouch and put a hand on his shoulder — he jolts, his whole body startled, and only once he sees it's you do his ears settle back down.

You spent that night reading.
It turns out he hadn't gotten stubborn.

Now you don't call his name from the doorway anymore.
You flip the light on first, so it sweeps across his eyes.
Before you reach him you tap the floor twice with your foot, so the vibration arrives before you do.
Dinner is a hand signal. A walk is you holding the leash up where he can see it.

He adapted faster than you did. You're the one who needed three months.

One evening you sit down beside him and he rests his chin on your leg.
And it occurs to you: he can't hear the world anymore.

He still waits by the door every single day.

Which means it was never the sound he was waiting for.
en.editorNote: Send to anyone whose dog has suddenly gotten "disobedient" in old age — get the ears checked, then change how you talk to him
variations: Short version: he didn't get stubborn, he went deaf. Dinner is a hand signal now, and I tap the floor twice before I reach him so the vibration gets there first.
Longer version: he can't hear the world anymore, and he still waits by the door every day. So it was never the sound he was waiting for.

items.sourceNote: 掃地機器人在寵物家庭的日常互動、機身鏡頭意外拍到狗狗的話題；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
家裡買了掃地機器人之後，多了一個編制外的員工。

機器一啟動，牠就從窩裡站起來，全程跟在後面三十公分，像個督工。

機器往左，牠往左。
機器卡在椅腳，牠低頭聞一下，然後抬頭看你，意思很清楚：你看，它又不行了。
機器回到充電座，牠也回窩趴下。收工。

最好笑的是那台有鏡頭。

某天你在辦公室無聊，點開清掃紀錄的影像，本來只是想確認地板乾不乾淨——

結果整段影片，就是一雙毛茸茸的腳掌，從第一分鐘跟到第四十分鐘。
中間還有一段是牠整隻趴下來，臉貼著地板，跟鏡頭對看了十秒。

那天你在辦公室笑到被同事轉頭看。

你買它的時候，是為了掃狗毛。

結果它變成家裡最貴的一個玩伴——而且是唯一一個，永遠不會喊累的那個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個家裡掃地機器人被狗當成同事的朋友——順便叫他去翻一下機器的錄影，笑點全都在裡面
variations: 精簡版：掃地機一啟動，牠就起身全程跟在後面三十公分。機器回充電座，牠也回窩趴下，收工。
延伸版：我買掃地機是為了掃狗毛，結果它變成家裡最貴的玩伴，而且是唯一一個永遠不會喊累的。

en.content:
Since the robot vacuum showed up, the household has an extra employee.

The second it starts, he gets out of bed and follows it at a steady one-foot distance, like a supervisor.

Robot goes left, he goes left.
Robot gets stuck on a chair leg, he sniffs it, then looks up at you — the meaning is unmistakable: see, it's useless again.
Robot docks itself, he goes back to his bed and lies down. Shift over.

The best part is that ours has a camera.

One slow afternoon at work you pull up the recording, meaning to check whether the floors got clean —

and the entire clip is a pair of fuzzy paws, minute one through minute forty.
Somewhere in the middle he flops down flat, puts his face on the floor, and stares into the lens for ten straight seconds.

You laughed hard enough that people turned around.

You bought it to deal with the shedding.

It turned into the most expensive playmate in the house — and the only one that never gets tired of him.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose dog treats the robot vacuum as a coworker, and tell them to go watch the camera footage
variations: Short version: the vacuum starts, he gets up and shadows it a foot behind the whole run. It docks, he goes back to bed. Shift over.
Longer version: I bought it for the shedding. It became the most expensive playmate in the house, and the only one that never gets tired of him.

items.sourceNote: 許多狗在陌生環境不願意上廁所、需要熟悉氣味定點的行為；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你帶牠回南部老家過三天。

第一天，院子那麼大，草那麼香，牠繞了七圈，每一根草都聞過，然後什麼都沒做，走回你腳邊坐下。

那天你帶牠出去四次。四次都一樣。

家人笑你想太多。你笑不出來，晚上還爬文爬到一點。

第二天清晨五點，牠終於在同一叢草前面投降了。
但你必須站在牠正前方，背對著牠，幫牠擋住整條巷子的視線，牠才肯蹲下去。

第三天下午，你們開車回台北。

車停好，電梯門一開，牠拉著你直奔巷口那根電線桿——就是那根，別根都不行——
然後停在那裡將近一分鐘，尾巴搖得像終於交差。

你蹲下來摸牠的頭，忽然想通一件事：

你以為家是你付房租的那個地方。

對牠來說，家是那根電線桿、那個轉角、那個味道，還有拿著牽繩的這隻手。

那三天牠不是不敢。

牠只是還沒到家。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個帶狗出遠門、一路上都在擔心「牠怎麼都不上廁所」的朋友——回到自家巷口就會自動解鎖
variations: 精簡版：回老家三天，院子那麼大牠什麼都不肯做；一回台北，電梯門一開就直奔巷口那根電線桿，別根都不行。
延伸版：我以為家是我付房租的地方。對牠來說，家是那根電線桿、那個轉角、那個味道，和拿著牽繩的這隻手。

en.content:
You take him to your parents' place for three days.

Day one: an enormous yard, grass everywhere. He does seven laps, sniffs every blade of it, does absolutely nothing, and comes back to sit at your feet.

You take him out four times. Four times, same result.

Your family says you're overthinking it. You are not laughing. You read forums until one in the morning.

Day two, five a.m., he finally caves at one specific clump of grass — but only if you stand directly in front of him with your back turned, blocking the view of the whole street.

Day three, you drive back to the city.

You park, the elevator opens, and he tows you straight to the utility pole at the corner — that one, no other pole will do —
and stays there for close to a minute, tail going like he's finally filed his report.

You crouch to scratch his head, and something clicks:

You thought home was the place you pay rent on.

For him, home is that pole, that corner, that smell, and the hand holding the leash.

He wasn't nervous for three days.

He just hadn't gotten home yet.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who took the dog on a trip and spent the whole time worrying about why he wouldn't go — the home block unlocks it
variations: Short version: three days away, huge yard, he refused to go. Back in the city the elevator opened and he made a beeline for the corner pole — that one, no other pole would do.
Longer version: I thought home was the place I pay rent on. For him it's that pole, that corner, that smell, and the hand holding the leash.

items.sourceNote: 飼主為毛孩開設專用存款帳戶（醫療預備金）的常見做法；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
櫃檯報出那個數字的時候，你「嗯」了一聲，卡就遞出去了。

你沒有看第二眼，也沒有算這個月還剩多少。
那筆帳，你是在回家的路上才開始算的。

隔週，你去銀行開了一個新帳戶。
那種可以自己取名字的。你在名稱欄輸入了牠的名字，後面加了「基金」兩個字。
設定每月一號自動轉一筆進去。

朋友知道以後笑你：牠又不會知道。

對，牠不會知道。

牠不知道那個帳戶存在，不知道自己每個月都被存了一筆錢，
更不知道上次牠全身麻醉洗牙的那天，你坐在診所外面的機車上，先深呼吸了三次才發得動車。

牠只知道你會回來接牠。

每一次都會。

所以那個帳戶你會一直存下去。

不是因為牠會知道，

是因為總有一天，你不想在最不該猶豫的那一秒，猶豫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個默默幫毛孩開了專屬帳戶的朋友，也適合提醒還沒開始存的人——今天開始都不算晚
variations: 精簡版：我開了一個新帳戶，名稱欄打了牠的名字加「基金」，每月一號自動轉。朋友笑我：牠又不會知道。對，牠不會知道。
延伸版：我存那筆錢不是因為牠會知道，是因為總有一天，我不想在最不該猶豫的那一秒猶豫。

en.content:
When the front desk read out the number, you said "okay" and handed over the card.

You didn't look at it twice and you didn't do the math on what was left this month.
You did that math later, on the way home.

The next week you opened a new savings account.
One of the kind you can nickname yourself. In the nickname field you typed his name and the word "fund."
Automatic transfer, first of every month.

A friend laughed when he heard: he'll never know.

Right. He'll never know.

He doesn't know the account exists. He doesn't know a little money goes in every month.
He definitely doesn't know that after his last dental cleaning under anesthesia, you sat outside the clinic and took three slow breaths before you could start the car.

All he knows is that you come back for him.

Every time.

So the account keeps growing.

Not because he'll ever know about it —

but because one day there will be a second where hesitating is the worst thing you could do, and you don't want to hesitate.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who quietly opened a savings account for their dog, and to anyone who hasn't started one yet — today still counts
variations: Short version: I opened a savings account, typed his name and the word "fund" in the nickname field, auto-transfer on the first. A friend laughed: he'll never know. Right. He'll never know.
Longer version: I'm not saving it because he'll ever know. I'm saving it because one day there'll be a second where I can't afford to hesitate.

items.sourceNote: 米克斯 DNA 檢測結果與飼主預期落差、報告末頁附帶藥物敏感基因標記的話題；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
收容所的認養卡上寫：疑似拉不拉多混米克斯，一歲。

你養了三年，被問過幾百次「這是什麼狗」。
你的標準答案是：「米克斯啦。」
問的人通常還會再追一句：「可是牠這個耳朵欸，是不是有混到什麼？」

於是你買了那個要在牠嘴巴裡刮三十秒的棉棒。

刮的時候牠一直想吃那根棉棒。你們摔角了四分鐘。

六個星期後，報告寄來。

你點開，往下滑。

牠的成分比你想像中誠實太多了——
最大宗的那一項，跟認養卡上寫的完全不一樣；
第二名是一個你要 Google 才知道長什麼樣子的品種；
再往下，有一欄直接寫「無法辨識的混種」，佔了百分之十五。

你笑到躺在沙發上。你家這隻狗，是一個委員會。

你把報告截圖傳到群組，大家開始亂猜哪個部分負責什麼：
挖沙發的是這個，看到腳踏車就發瘋的是那個，
半夜十一點在客廳自己繞圈的，應該是那百分之十五。

但你真正看了兩遍的，是報告最後面那一頁。

那頁沒有品種，只有一串健康標記。
其中一項寫著：某一類常見的藥物，對牠可能有風險。

你把那一頁存下來，設成手機裡的最愛。
下一次帶牠看病，那張圖會比任何一句話先出現。

那天你才發現，你花錢買的不是牠的身世。

是牠下一次躺在診療台上的時候，你能替牠說的那句話。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個養米克斯、每次被問「這什麼狗」都答不出來的朋友——順便提醒他，報告最後那頁健康標記才是重點
variations: 精簡版：報告出來，最大宗那項跟認養卡上寫的完全不一樣，還有一欄直接寫「無法辨識的混種」佔百分之十五。我家這隻狗是一個委員會。
延伸版：我花錢買的不是牠的身世，是牠下次躺在診療台上的時候，我能替牠說的那句話。

en.content:
The shelter card said: Labrador mix, approximately one year old.

Three years in, you have been asked what kind of dog he is a few hundred times.
Your stock answer is "he's a mutt."
The follow-up is almost always: "but look at those ears — there's something else in there, right?"

So you bought the kit with the swab you're supposed to hold in his mouth for thirty seconds.

He spent all thirty of those seconds trying to eat the swab. It took four minutes.

Six weeks later the report lands in your inbox.

You open it and scroll.

The mix is far more honest than you were ready for.
The biggest slice is nothing like what the shelter card said.
Second place is a breed you have to look up to find out what it even looks like.
Further down, one line just reads "unresolved mixed breed" and gives it fifteen percent.

You laughed until you were lying flat on the couch. Your dog is a committee.

You screenshot it into the group chat and everyone starts assigning blame:
the couch-digging is clearly this one, the losing-his-mind-at-bicycles is that one,
and the eleven p.m. laps around the living room are definitely the fifteen percent.

But the page you actually read twice is the last one.

No breeds on that page. Just a list of health markers.
One of them says a common class of medication could be risky for him.

You saved that page and favorited it on your phone.
Next vet visit, that screenshot goes up before anything else does.

That's when it hit you: you didn't pay to find out where he came from.

You paid for the sentence you'll be able to say on his behalf, next time he's on the exam table.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend with a rescue mutt who can never answer "what is he?" — and tell them the health-marker page at the end is the part that matters
variations: Short version: the report came back and the biggest slice was nothing like what the shelter card said, plus fifteen percent labeled "unresolved mixed breed." My dog is a committee.
Longer version: I didn't pay to find out where he came from. I paid for the sentence I'll be able to say for him next time he's on the exam table.

items.sourceNote: 高齡犬水中跑步機復健、寵物長照照護設施在台推廣的相關報導；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
醫生說的是「後腳的肌肉在流失」，不是「牠老了」。

差別很大。前者，有事情可以做。

於是你每個星期三下午請兩小時假，帶牠去一個有水的房間。

那是一台像玻璃箱的跑步機，水會慢慢注到牠胸口的高度。

第一次牠嚇壞了。四隻腳撐得死緊，整隻僵在原地，眼睛隔著玻璃直直看你。
你蹲下來，臉貼在玻璃外面，一直跟牠說話。你不記得說了什麼，反正沒停過。

第三分鐘，牠踏出了第一步。

水的浮力會替牠拿掉大半的體重，所以在裡面，牠可以走得比在地面上久好幾倍。
第一次走了四分鐘。第四次走了十一分鐘。

上個月牠走了二十分鐘，出來的時候自己抖乾，把整間治療室的人都噴到。

回家的路上你忽然想到一件事。

你們一起走過那麼多路——河堤、公園、巷子、你搬過的三個地方。
每一段，都是牠在前面拉著你走。

現在換你在玻璃外面蹲著，陪牠走完這幾百公尺。

牠還是每一次都會回頭確認你在。

那就慢慢走吧。慢的也是走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給家裡狗狗後腳開始無力的朋友——「牠老了」跟「肌肉在流失」是兩件事，後者有事情可以做
variations: 精簡版：第一次進水中跑步機牠嚇到四腳僵住，只隔著玻璃看我。第三分鐘牠踏出第一步，上個月牠在裡面走了二十分鐘。
延伸版：以前每一段路都是牠在前面拉著我走。現在換我蹲在玻璃外面，陪牠走完這幾百公尺。慢的也是走。

en.content:
The vet said "he's losing muscle in his hind end," not "he's old."

The difference matters, because the first one comes with something you can do.

So every Wednesday afternoon you take two hours off and drive him to a room with water in it.

It's a treadmill inside a glass tank. The water rises slowly to about chest height on him.

The first session terrified him. All four legs locked, whole body rigid, eyes fixed on you through the glass.
You crouched with your face against the outside of the tank and talked. You don't remember what about. You just didn't stop.

At the three-minute mark, he took a step.

The buoyancy takes most of his weight off, so in there he can walk many times longer than he can on the ground.
Four minutes that first day. Eleven by the fourth session.

Last month he did twenty, then shook himself off on the way out and soaked every person in the room.

On the drive home, something occurred to you.

All the miles the two of you have covered — the river path, the park, the alley, three different apartments —
he was always out in front, towing you along.

Now you're the one on the other side of the glass, crouched down, walking the last few hundred meters with him.

He still checks over his shoulder every time, to make sure you're there.

So: slowly, then. Slow still counts as walking.
en.editorNote: Send to anyone whose dog's back legs are starting to give out — "he's old" and "he's losing muscle" are not the same diagnosis
variations: Short version: first hydrotherapy session he locked up completely and just stared at me through the glass. Three minutes in, he took a step. Last month he walked twenty.
Longer version: he spent his whole life out in front, towing me along. Now I'm the one crouched outside the glass, walking the last few hundred meters with him.

items.sourceNote: 寵物錄音溝通按鈕（talking buttons）在飼主社群的流行與實際使用狀況；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你在網路上看到有人教狗踩按鈕講話，於是買了四顆。

每一顆可以錄一句你自己的聲音。
你很認真地規劃了牠的第一組詞彙：
「外面」、「吃飯」、「玩」、「摸摸」。

你花了三個星期，每次出門前都自己先踩一次「外面」，再帶牠下樓。

第十九天，牠學會了。

牠學會了「外面」。

然後你的人生就結束了。

早上六點四十：外面。
你嘴裡還含著牙刷：外面。
剛從外面回來，牽繩還在你手上：外面。
下雨天你說今天不出去，牠走過去，很慢、很清楚地：外面。外面。外面。

另外三顆，三個月來牠一次都沒有碰過。

不是不會。你把「吃飯」搬到飯碗旁邊，牠聞了聞，然後走去踩「外面」。

有天晚上你坐在地板上很認真地問牠：你可不可以踩點別的？
牠聽完，走過去，踩了「外面」。

後來你把那三顆收起來了。留一顆就好。

因為你發現，牠不是只會一句。

牠是把唯一一次能對你開口的機會，
拿來要同一件事：

「我們一起出去。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在教狗踩錄音按鈕說話的朋友——先做好心理準備，牠只會學會對他最有效的那一顆
variations: 精簡版：買了四顆錄音按鈕，牠只學會「外面」。我問牠可不可以踩點別的，牠聽完走過去，踩了「外面」。
延伸版：牠不是只會一句。牠是把唯一一次能對我開口的機會，拿來要同一件事：我們一起出去。

en.content:
You saw the videos of dogs pressing buttons to talk, so you bought four of them.

Each one records a phrase in your own voice.
You put real thought into his starter vocabulary:
OUTSIDE. DINNER. PLAY. PETS.

For three weeks you pressed OUTSIDE yourself before every single walk, then took him down.

Day nineteen, he got it.

He got OUTSIDE.

And that was the end of your life as you knew it.

6:40 a.m.: outside.
You, mid-toothbrush: outside.
Twelve seconds back from a walk, leash still in your hand: outside.
Rainy day, you say not today — he walks over and, slowly and very clearly: outside. outside. outside.

The other three buttons have not been touched in three months.

It isn't that he can't. You moved DINNER next to his bowl. He sniffed it, then went and pressed OUTSIDE.

One night you sat on the floor and asked him, sincerely, whether he could press literally anything else.
He listened, walked over, and pressed OUTSIDE.

Eventually you put the other three away. One is enough.

Because you figured out he doesn't only know one word.

He got exactly one chance to say something to you,
and he spends it asking for the same thing every time:

let's go out, together.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend teaching their dog talking buttons — warn them the dog will master exactly one, and it will be the one that works on them
variations: Short version: bought four talking buttons, he learned OUTSIDE and only OUTSIDE. I asked him if he could press anything else. He walked over and pressed OUTSIDE.
Longer version: he doesn't only know one word. He got one chance to say something to me, and he spends it asking for the same thing: let's go out, together.

items.sourceNote: 夏季犬隻遭蜂螫導致顏面腫脹、需盡速就醫的常見獸醫衛教情境；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
牠在公園裡對著一叢開花的灌木，做出你這輩子看過最專業的撲擊姿勢。

前腳一壓，屁股翹高，然後跳。

你「不要」還沒喊出口，牠已經完成了。

回家路上牠很得意，走路都在跳。

進門十五分鐘後，你抬頭看牠一眼，然後整個人從沙發上彈起來。

牠的右半邊臉，腫成了左半邊的一點五倍。

你抓了牽繩、鑰匙，還有自己的健保卡（對，你抓了自己的），衝去動物醫院。

醫生看了兩秒，說了四個字：「被蜂螫了。」
打一針，觀察三十分鐘，回家。

那三十分鐘裡，牠坐在診間地板上，用那張歪掉的臉，
對每一個經過的人搖尾巴。

醫生說很多狗都會這樣，然後補了一句：
「牠們通常不會學乖。」

你問：那通常多久會再來一次？

醫生笑了：「看牠多久遇到下一朵花。」

現在你們家散步多了一條規則。

看到開花的灌木，繞路。

牠每一次都會回頭看那叢花一眼，那個眼神你很熟——

那不是害怕。

那是「下次」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個狗狗在公園什麼都要咬一口的朋友——臉突然腫起來要立刻就醫，而且牠真的不會學乖
variations: 精簡版：牠對著一叢花做出畢生最專業的撲擊，十五分鐘後右臉腫成左臉的一點五倍。醫生說：牠們通常不會學乖。
延伸版：現在看到開花的灌木我們就繞路。牠每次都會回頭看一眼，那個眼神不是害怕，是「下次」。

en.content:
He hit a flowering bush with the most technically perfect pounce you have ever witnessed.

Front end down, back end up, launch.

You did not get the word "no" out in time.

He was extremely pleased with himself the whole way home. Bouncing.

Fifteen minutes after you got in the door you glanced over at him and came off the couch like you'd been ejected.

The right side of his face was about one and a half times the size of the left side.

You grabbed the leash, the keys, and your own wallet, and drove to the emergency vet.

She looked at him for two seconds and said three words: "He got stung."
One injection, thirty minutes of observation, go home.

For those thirty minutes he sat on the floor of the exam room and wagged at every single person who walked past, with his crooked face.

She said a lot of dogs do this, and then added:
"They generally don't learn."

You asked how long until it happens again.

She laughed. "Depends how soon he meets his next flower."

Your walks have a new rule now.

Flowering bush, cross the street.

He looks back at every one of them, and you know that look.

It isn't fear.

It's "next time."
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose dog mouths everything at the park — sudden facial swelling is an emergency vet trip, and no, he will not learn
variations: Short version: he pounced on a flowering bush and fifteen minutes later the right side of his face was half again the size of the left. The vet said dogs generally don't learn.
Longer version: we cross the street for flowering bushes now. He looks back at every one, and that look isn't fear — it's "next time."

items.sourceNote: 犬隻換糧建議以七天漸進混合、突然換糧容易軟便的常見衛教說明；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
「換飼料要循序漸進，第一天先混一成新的就好。」

你照做。倒進碗裡，攪拌均勻，還特地用湯匙壓過一遍，確保看不出來。

牠走過來，低頭聞三秒。

然後開始一場外科手術。

牠用舌頭把舊飼料一顆一顆挑起來吃掉，新的那幾顆原封不動留在碗底，排得整整齊齊，像證物。

你站在旁邊看著那一成，第一次真心懷疑自己的智商。

第二天你把比例降到半成。牠還是挑得出來。

第三天你淋了一點無鹽雞湯。牠把湯舔乾淨，飼料原地不動。

第四天你放棄科學，蹲在碗前面假裝吃得很享受。牠歪頭看你，眼神有點擔心。

第七天，牠把整碗吃完了。

你興奮到想拍照。

然後你發現——那是舊飼料。你昨天分裝的時候拿錯袋子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在跟狗打換糧持久戰的朋友——七天是給牠的腸胃用的，不是給你的自尊心用的
variations: 精簡版：換糧第一天只混了一成新飼料，牠低頭聞三秒，然後用舌頭把舊的一顆一顆挑起來吃掉，新的留在碗底排得整整齊齊，像證物。
延伸版：第七天牠終於把整碗吃完，我興奮到想拍照。後來才發現那是舊飼料——我前一晚分裝的時候拿錯袋子了。

en.content:
Kibble transitions come with an official schedule: day one is ten percent new food, ninety percent old.

You follow it. Pour, stir, press it flat with a spoon so the new pieces don't show.

He walks over. Sniffs for three seconds.

Then he performs surgery.

He tongues out the old pieces one at a time and leaves the new ones sitting at the bottom of the bowl, untouched, lined up like evidence.

You stand there looking at that ten percent and question your own intelligence for the first time in years.

Day two you drop it to five percent. He still finds them.

Day three you add a splash of unsalted broth. He licks the bowl dry and leaves the kibble exactly where it was.

Day four you abandon science and crouch next to the bowl pretending to enjoy it yourself. He tilts his head at you, mildly concerned.

Day seven, he cleans the whole bowl.

You reach for your phone to document it.

Then you realize it was the old food. You grabbed the wrong bag when you portioned it out last night.
en.editorNote: Send to anyone currently losing a food-transition war — the seven-day rule is for the dog's stomach, not the owner's pride
variations: Short version: day one was ten percent new kibble. He sniffed for three seconds, then tongued out every old piece and left the new ones at the bottom of the bowl like evidence.
Longer version: day seven he finished the whole bowl and I reached for my phone. Then I realized it was the old food — I'd grabbed the wrong bag the night before.

items.sourceNote: 台灣垃圾車定時定點播放音樂、犬隻對固定聲音形成時間預期的日常觀察；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
巷子口那台垃圾車，每天晚上七點二十分經過。

牠比垃圾車還準。

七點十八分，牠會從沙發上坐起來。耳朵先動，然後整隻狗轉向大門，像一台開始暖機的機器。

七點十九分，你什麼都還沒聽到，牠已經走到玄關站好。

七點二十分，〈少女的祈禱〉從巷子另一頭飄過來。

牠回頭看你一眼，那個眼神翻譯出來是：「我不是講過了嗎。」

問題是，你們家的垃圾是早上拿去定點回收的。

牠一次都沒有跟去過。

牠只是發現這件事每天都會發生，就認定那應該跟牠有關。

有些班沒有人排，也沒有人驗收。牠自己認領了，然後準時上工三年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個狗比垃圾車還準時的朋友——牠不知道那是什麼，但牠很確定那是牠的班
variations: 精簡版：垃圾車七點二十到，牠七點十八就從沙發坐起來走到玄關站好。我什麼都還沒聽到，牠已經回頭用「我不是講過了嗎」的眼神看我。
延伸版：我們家的垃圾是早上丟的，牠一次都沒跟去過。但牠還是每天七點十八分準時上工——有些班是牠自己排給自己的。

en.content:
Garbage trucks here play music. Ours turns into the alley at 7:20 every night with a tinny little piano tune.

He is more punctual than the truck.

7:18, he sits up on the couch. Ears move first, then the whole dog rotates toward the front door like a machine spinning up.

7:19, you still can't hear a thing. He's already standing in the entryway, in position.

7:20, the piano tune drifts in from the far end of the alley.

He looks back at you, and the look translates roughly to: I did tell you.

Here's the thing. We take our trash to the morning drop-off point instead.

He has never once come along.

He just noticed this happens every single day, and concluded it must be his.

Some shifts nobody assigns and nobody signs off on. He claimed this one himself and hasn't missed it in three years.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose dog runs on the garbage truck's schedule — he has no idea what it is, but he is certain it's his shift
variations: Short version: the truck hits our alley at 7:20 and he's off the couch and standing at the door by 7:18, before I can hear anything at all.
Longer version: we use the morning drop-off, so he has never once gone with us. He clocks in at 7:18 anyway. Some shifts you assign yourself.

items.sourceNote: 犬隻散步途中定住不肯前進（俗稱「當機」）的常見行為情境；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
散步走到一半，牠會突然變成一袋水泥。

沒有預兆。前一秒還走得好好的，下一秒牠在人行道正中央坐下，四隻腳往地上一釘，眼睛看向某個你完全看不出有什麼的方向。

你拉牽繩，牠的重量瞬間變成三倍。

你蹲下來講道理，牠聽完，繼續看那個方向。

你拿出零食，牠吃掉，然後坐回原位。

你假裝要走了，走出五公尺回頭——牠還在。而且牠很確定你會回來。

最後你抱著牠走了半條巷子，旁邊等紅燈的騎士全程看著你。

轉角一過，牠開始扭。你把牠放下來。

牠立刻變回一隻正常的狗，尾巴翹著走在最前面帶路，好像剛剛那五分鐘是你自己編出來的。

過了一年你才發現，牠每次都停在同一個地方。

那是路線轉向回家的那個轉角。

牠不是走不動。牠是還沒散完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個抱過狗走完最後半條巷子的朋友——下次看一下牠停在哪，答案通常就在那個轉角
variations: 精簡版：牠散步到一半會突然變成一袋水泥。拉牽繩，體重瞬間變三倍；給零食，牠吃完坐回原位；假裝要走，牠很確定你會回來。
延伸版：過了一年我才發現，牠每次都停在同一個轉角——那是路線轉回家的地方。牠不是走不動，牠是還沒散完。

en.content:
Sidewalk strikes are real. Halfway through the walk he turns into a bag of cement.

No warning. One second he's trotting along, the next he's sitting in the middle of the sidewalk with all four feet nailed down, staring at something you cannot see.

You pull the leash. His body weight instantly triples.

You crouch down and reason with him. He hears you out and goes back to staring.

You produce a treat. He eats it and sits back down.

You pretend to leave, get five meters away, look back — still there. And fully confident you're coming back.

You end up carrying him half a block while a guy waiting at the light watches the entire performance.

Around the corner he starts squirming. You put him down.

He instantly becomes a normal dog again, tail up, out in front, leading the way, like the last five minutes were something you invented.

It took a year to notice he stops in the same spot every time.

It's the corner where the route turns toward home.

He isn't tired. He just isn't finished.
en.editorNote: Send to anyone who's carried a stubborn dog the last half block — check where he stops next time, the answer is usually that corner
variations: Short version: he becomes a bag of cement mid-walk. Pull the leash and his weight triples. Offer a treat and he eats it, then sits back down.
Longer version: took me a year to notice he stops at the same corner every time — the one where the route turns toward home. He isn't tired, he just isn't finished.

items.sourceNote: 中秋節寵物照護提醒：柚子皮所含柑橘油可能刺激犬貓皮膚與呼吸道；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
中秋還有七個禮拜，月餅連打折的季節都還沒到。

但你已經在手機相簿裡往回翻去年那張照片了。

照片裡牠戴著柚子皮帽，眼睛半閉，表情是那種「我配合你，但我們心知肚明」的表情。

今年你本來想拍個升級版。

然後你查了才知道，柚子皮上的柑橘油會刺激狗的皮膚跟呼吸道，那個味道對牠的鼻子來說，濃度大概是你聞到的一百倍。

難怪牠去年那個表情是那樣。

所以計畫改了。

你在網路上找到一頂棉的、圓的、黃黃的、離兩公尺遠看很像柚子皮的帽子。它已經在購物車裡躺了一個禮拜，因為你在等節前那一波折扣。

離中秋還有七個禮拜。

你不是在期待連假。

你是在期待一張照片。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每年中秋都要幫狗喬造型的朋友——柚子皮的柑橘油會刺激皮膚跟呼吸道，換一頂棉的，照片一樣可愛
variations: 精簡版：離中秋還有七個禮拜，月餅連打折都還沒開始，我已經在翻去年那張柚子皮帽的照片了。
延伸版：查了才知道柚子皮的柑橘油會刺激狗的皮膚跟呼吸道。今年改買一頂棉的，離兩公尺遠看很像——牠去年那個表情，我現在懂了。

en.content:
Pomelo hats are the tradition here: you carve the peel into a little cap and put it on the dog for Mid-Autumn.

The festival is still seven weeks out. Mooncakes aren't even on sale yet.

But you're already scrolling back to last year's photo. He's wearing the peel, eyes half closed, doing the expression that says: I'm cooperating, but we both know what this is.

You were planning a bigger version this year.

Then you looked it up. The citrus oil in the peel irritates a dog's skin and airways, and that smell reaches his nose at roughly a hundred times the strength it reaches yours.

Which explains the expression.

So the plan changed.

You found a cotton hat online — round, yellow, close enough from two meters away. It's been sitting in your cart for a week because you're waiting for the pre-holiday discount.

Seven weeks to go.

You're not counting down to the long weekend.

You're counting down to one photo.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who styles their dog for every holiday — pomelo peel oil irritates skin and airways, and a cotton hat gets you the same photo
variations: Short version: seven weeks to Mid-Autumn, mooncakes aren't even discounted yet, and I'm already scrolling back to last year's pomelo-hat photo.
Longer version: turns out the citrus oil in the peel irritates their skin and airways. Cotton hat this year — looks the same from two meters. Now I understand last year's expression.

items.sourceNote: 伊莉莎白項圈照護資訊：會影響行動與方向感、容易撞到牆與家具、進食需墊高碗或改用淺盤、通常戴到拆線或傷口癒合；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
「戴七到十四天，拆線前不可以自己拿掉。」

獸醫講這句話的時候你點頭點得很快，心想兩個禮拜而已。

第一個小時你就知道自己低估了。

牠不會倒退。前進沒問題，但只要頭套卡進沙發跟茶几中間，牠就停在那裡維持前傾的姿勢，等你去救。那個晚上你救了九次。

吃飯也出事。碗太深，頭套先碰到碗底，嘴巴還離飼料三公分。你把碗墊高，換成淺盤，牠才吃到第一口。

但最讓你受不了的不是這些。

是聲音。

走過走廊，塑膠邊緣刮到牆；轉進廚房，刮到冰箱；擠過門縫，刮到門框。整個家變成一張聲納圖，你閉著眼睛都知道牠在哪一格。

第十二天，醫生說可以拆了。

你剪開束帶的那一刻，牠甩甩頭，跑得比誰都快。

那天晚上，家裡安靜到你不太習慣。

你躺在床上聽了很久，什麼都沒聽到。

於是你起身走到客廳看牠一眼。

牠好好的，在自己的窩裡睡得很沉。

你才發現，那兩個禮拜你煩的其實不是噪音。

是你第一次，隨時都知道牠在哪裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在陪狗度過術後頭套期的朋友——碗墊高、換成淺盤會好很多，上下樓梯記得盯著點，時間長短一定要照醫生說的來
variations: 精簡版：牠戴頭套那兩個禮拜，塑膠刮到牆、刮到冰箱、刮到門框，整個家變成一張聲納圖。拆掉的那天晚上，安靜到我不習慣。
延伸版：碗太深，頭套先碰到碗底，嘴巴還離飼料三公分——把碗墊高、換成淺盤，牠才吃到第一口。這種小事沒人會先告訴你。

en.content:
"Seven to fourteen days. Don't take it off before the stitches come out."

You nodded fast at the vet. Two weeks. Fine.

Within the first hour you knew you'd underestimated it.

He can't reverse. Forward is fine, but the moment the cone wedges between the couch and the coffee table, he just stops there, leaning forward, waiting to be rescued. You rescued him nine times that night.

Meals were a problem too. The bowl was too deep — the cone hit the bottom while his mouth was still an inch above the food. You had to raise the bowl and switch to a shallow plate before he got a single bite.

But none of that was the part that got to you.

It was the sound.

Down the hallway, plastic scraping the wall. Into the kitchen, scraping the fridge. Through a half-open door, scraping the frame. The whole apartment turned into a sonar map, and you could locate him with your eyes shut.

Day twelve, the vet cleared it.

The second you cut the strap he shook his head out and ran like he'd been saving it up.

That night the place was quiet in a way you weren't used to.

You lay in bed listening for a long time and heard nothing.

So you got up and went to check on him.

He was fine. In his own bed, out cold.

And that's when it landed: those two weeks, the thing bothering you was never the noise.

It was the first time you always knew exactly where he was.
en.editorNote: Send to a friend nursing a dog through the cone period — raise the bowl, use a shallow plate, watch them on stairs, and follow the vet's timeline on when it comes off
variations: Short version: two weeks in the cone — plastic scraping the wall, the fridge, the doorframe. The night it came off, the apartment was too quiet.

Longer version: the bowl was too deep, so the cone hit the bottom while his mouth was still an inch above the food. Raised bowl, shallow plate, and he finally ate. Nobody tells you that part in advance.

items.sourceNote: 寵物攝影技巧整理：寵物好動需高速快門與連續對焦、善用連拍再挑選；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你手機裡有四千多張牠的照片。

清楚的，大概不到十分之一。

原因你很清楚：只要你舉起手機，牠就會動。而且不是隨便動，是精準地在快門按下去的前零點二秒抬頭、轉身、往你這邊衝過來。

所以你收藏了一整批傑作：

一團會發光的白色殘影。
半張臉，另外半張是空氣。
四隻腳都在畫面裡，頭不在。
一個鼻孔的特寫，佔滿整個螢幕，還帶著水氣。

你試過連拍。三十張裡面，二十九張是不同角度的模糊。
你試過鎖定對焦。它鎖定了地板。
你甚至下載了那個號稱能偵測寵物臉的 App。它把你的拖鞋認成狗。

真正清楚的那幾張，全部只有一種情況：牠睡著的時候。

某天你整理相簿，本來想把糊掉的刪一刪。

你選了三百多張，手指停在刪除上面，然後退出來了。

因為你看著那些殘影，突然想到——

會糊，是因為牠在動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個相簿裡九成是糊掉的狗照的朋友——先別急著刪，那些殘影是牠現在還跑得動的證據
variations: 精簡版：我手機裡四千張狗的照片，清楚的不到十分之一。原因很簡單：只要我舉起手機，牠就會動。
延伸版：本來要刪掉三百張糊照，手指停在刪除鍵上又退出來了——會糊，是因為牠在動。

en.content:
There are four thousand photos of him on your phone.

Maybe one in ten is in focus.

You know why. The instant you lift the phone, he moves — and not randomly. He times it, head up and body turning about two-tenths of a second before the shutter fires.

So you own a whole gallery of masterpieces:

A glowing white smear.
Half a face; the other half is air.
All four legs in frame, head not included.
One nostril, filling the entire screen, slightly damp.

You tried burst mode. Twenty-nine of thirty came out blurry from thirty different angles.
You tried locking the focus. It locked onto the floor.
You even downloaded the app that claims to detect pet faces. It identified your slipper as a dog.

The genuinely sharp ones all have one thing in common: he's asleep.

One evening you sat down to clean out the camera roll.

You selected three hundred blurry ones, hovered over delete, and backed out.

Because you looked at all that motion blur and thought —

it's blurry because he's moving.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose camera roll is 90% blurry dog — don't delete them, the blur is proof he still runs like that
variations: Short version: four thousand photos of my dog, fewer than one in ten in focus. Simple reason: the second I lift the phone, he moves.
Longer version: I selected three hundred blurry ones, hovered over delete, and backed out. It's blurry because he's moving.

items.sourceNote: 居家寵物清潔資訊：家具底下與縫隙是毛髮與雜物累積的死角，建議定期移開清理；情境與文字皆為原創

zh-tw.content:
你今天心血來潮，決定把沙發搬開，好好掃一次底下。

出土文物如下：

三顆不同時期的球。
一隻襪子，你的，另一隻還在抽屜裡等了兩年。
半根潔牙骨，被咬成一個很有想法的形狀。
一片玩具碎片，本體早就丟了。
一個你完全不認得的東西。你研究了三秒，決定不要繼續研究。
還有毛。非常、非常多的毛。

你把這些東西排在地板上，排得像考古分類。

牠走過來，一件一件聞。

然後叼起其中一顆球，跳上沙發，往牠固定的那個角落一躺，兩隻前腳把球夾好。

那顆球，是去年冬天你找了一整晚、最後認定「一定是散步的時候掉了」的那一顆。

你們一起找到你放棄。

牠一直知道它在哪裡。

牠只是從來沒想過，這件事需要告訴你。
